definitions.gloss: (not) at all; (not) in the least; by no means
definitions.explanation: Used with negative forms to emphasize that something has not happened or changed at all, despite expectations.

examples.japanese: {一向|いっこう}に{気|き}にしない。
{雨|あめ}が{一向|いっこう}に{止|や}まない。
examples.english: The rain shows no sign of stopping.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{説明|せつめい}しても{一向|いっこう}に{理解|りかい}してくれないので、{困|こま}っている。
examples.english: No matter how many times I explain, they don't understand at all, which is frustrating.

notes:
Almost always used with a negative verb or adjective in the pattern {一向|いっこう}に + negative. Expresses frustration or emphasis that something has completely failed to change or happen. Stronger than simply using ない alone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一向|いっこう}に{構|かま}わない: I don't mind at all
- {一向|いっこう}に{変|か}わらない: hasn't changed at all
- {一向|いっこう}に{進|すす}まない: making no progress at all
- {一向|いっこう}に{止|や}まない: shows no sign of stopping
- {一向|いっこう}に{気|き}にしない: don't care at all

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {全然|ぜんぜん}: not at all — more casual, used in everyday speech
- {全|まった}く: not at all, completely — similar emphasis but more versatile
- {少|すこ}しも: not even a little — emphasizes the complete absence of something
- ちっとも: not at all — casual, often expresses complaint or frustration
